title: Cumulative retrieval quiz on the three biographies
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy
source: Seeded from english/y7 lesson 73 (Cumulative retrieval quiz on the three biographies (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 62 to 77 of Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Ali lost three and a half years of his career rather than go against his beliefs. What does this show?
questions.a: B) conviction. Giving up so much for a belief shows conviction: a firmly held principle guiding his actions.

questions.q: What is the writer's main viewpoint?
questions.a: C) Perseverance matters more than talent. The final sentences say perseverance, not giftedness, is the real question.

questions.q: What does 'unbroken' suggest about Ali?
questions.a: A) his spirit survived great pressure. Unbroken implies something that faced force but did not break: his will, not his body.

questions.q: Which is a precise DIRT improvement?
options: Add a Zoom in on 'unbroken' and explain its connotation
questions.a: B) Add a Zoom in on 'unbroken' and explain its connotation. A precise improvement names a specific skill to add.

questions.q: Why might a ruler of a huge state choose patched clothes?
options: because he had no money at all
to stay humble and close to ordinary people
questions.a: C) to stay humble and close to ordinary people. Choosing simplicity while holding power shows humility and solidarity with the people.

questions.q: Which sentence links best after: 'Umar asked governors to explain their wealth.'?
options: This shows he held others to the same standard he held himself.
Umar asked governors to explain their wealth.
questions.a: A) This shows he held others to the same standard he held himself.. 'This shows' uses a pronoun to refer back and develops the idea; the others repeat or break the link.

questions.q: Q6 is worth 8 marks. How long should you spend?
questions.a: B) about 12 to 15 minutes. More marks means more time; about a minute and a half per mark here.

questions.q: Which plan is most useful for Task B?
options: Intro view; 3 PEEDL points: practice, failure, Ali; counter; conclusion
questions.a: C) Intro view; 3 PEEDL points: practice, failure, Ali; counter; conclusion. A plan with a clear view, points and a counter-argument structures the article.

questions.q: What does Khalid's loyal service after being replaced as commander show?
options: he served the cause, not his own status
he was not a good leader
questions.a: A) he served the cause, not his own status. Accepting a lower position without complaint shows his service was for Allah and the community, not for status.

questions.q: What does 'a legacy is less a monument than a seed' suggest?
options: legacy grows in other people over time
questions.a: B) legacy grows in other people over time. A seed grows into something new; a monument stays still. The writer means legacy lives on through others.

questions.q: Which correctly fixes 'Ali was banned, he did not give up.'?
options: Ali was banned he did not give up.
Ali was banned, he, did not give up.
Ali was banned, but he did not give up.
questions.a: C) Ali was banned, but he did not give up.. Adding the conjunction 'but' correctly joins the two clauses.

questions.q: Which is the most precise Year 8 target?
options: Zoom in on one word in every analytical paragraph
questions.a: A) Zoom in on one word in every analytical paragraph. It names one checkable skill.

questions.q: What most improves a 'retelling' answer?
options: zoom in on a word and explain its effect
questions.a: B) zoom in on a word and explain its effect. Analysis comes from explaining the effect of specific words.

questions.q: Which redraft best improves 'The sea was very rough and scary.'?
options: The sea was very, very rough.
The sea was rough and scary and big.
The sea hurled itself at the rocks.
questions.a: C) The sea hurled itself at the rocks.. A precise verb (hurled) and personification replace vague adjectives.

questions.q: Why choose only three events?
options: to focus on what reveals character
questions.a: A) to focus on what reveals character. Biographers select events that show who the person really is.

questions.q: Which sentence best presents her generosity?
options: She gave them her savings without a word.
questions.a: B) She gave them her savings without a word.. Showing the action, and that she did it quietly, presents generosity better than telling.

questions.q: A biography is written...
questions.a: A) by someone else about a real person
options: by someone else about a real person

questions.q: Chronological means...
questions.a: A) in time order

questions.q: Which is a feature of non-fiction?
questions.a: A) facts and dates

questions.q: A biography is usually written in...
questions.a: B) the third person
